work.heading: A few things I kept thinking about until I built them.

titiplo.title: TITIPLO
titiplo.description: I kept wondering why jastip businesses still run almost everything from chat. What started as a small prototype became a seller app, buyer storefront, order flow, payment proof system, and subscription product.

loss.title: Loss of Sales Dashboard
loss.description: OOS, stock history, sales velocity, and lost-sales estimates in one place.
loss.intro: This started because checking OOS, stock history, and potential lost sales manually was taking too much time.
loss.problem: Stock history, sales velocity, OOS dates, and lost-sales estimates were spread across different sheets and calculations.
loss.approach: I pulled those pieces into one flow, then kept simplifying the dashboard around the questions I actually needed answered.
loss.outcome: A much clearer way to see which SKUs are actually causing operational and sales impact.

nfc.title: NFC Review System
nfc.description: A small physical-product experiment using NFC, QR, and unique activation.
nfc.intro: I wanted to see if a cheap NFC tag could become a small product instead of just a tech demo.
nfc.problem: A simple tap card is easy to copy conceptually, so it needed its own identity, activation flow, and destination setup.
nfc.approach: Each card gets a unique serial, an activation step, and a simple routing layer behind the tap.
nfc.outcome: A reusable physical + digital product idea that can be produced cheaply and configured per customer.

commerce.title: E-commerce Automation
commerce.description: Scripts, calculators, and workflows made because repeating work gets boring.
commerce.intro: Not one project, but a growing collection of shortcuts I built because I did not want to repeat the same work every day.
commerce.problem: Pricing, fees, stock checks, reporting, and marketplace calculations are repetitive and easy to get wrong.
commerce.approach: Whenever a task repeated often enough, I tried to turn it into a formula, calculator, script, or lightweight workflow.
commerce.outcome: Less repetitive admin, fewer manual calculations, and faster day-to-day operations.

anti.title: Android Anti-Theft
anti.description: A side experiment with unlock triggers, capture flow, and location alerts.
anti.intro: This was mostly curiosity: what could an Android device do automatically after a suspicious unlock attempt?
anti.problem: A stolen or lost phone becomes much harder to trace once somebody starts trying to access it.
anti.approach: I experimented with failed-unlock triggers, camera capture, device location, and remote alerts.
anti.outcome: A working proof of concept and a good excuse to learn more about Android device behavior.

quote.text: “Most problems don’t need a bigger system. They usually need a simpler one.”
quote.sign: — Bayu, after overcomplicating a few of them first.

about.heading: I didn’t start with code.
about.lead: I started in sales and marketplace operations. Then spreadsheets got complicated, reporting got slow, and repetitive work kept piling up.
paragraphs: So I learned enough formulas to fix one problem. Then Apps Script for another. Then JavaScript, Cloudflare, Android, and whatever else the next problem needed.
I still don’t think of myself as “a developer first.” I’m more interested in understanding how work actually happens, then making it less annoying.
